utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, incidentally, which UNMOs were providing you with this information?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a Canadian UNMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Captain Dave McDonald?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Flynn, I think -- can I look in my --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it was Captain Flynn and it was a Canadian -- a captain, and Captain Zoutendijk, a Dutch captain, but it was Captain Flynn who gave those reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Then on the next page from which it comes, 3455, if you could read paragraph D, please.

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: "D. Serb offensive is not an offensive in the classical sense. It consists of slow steady and deliberate shelling of front line villages. The population flee as they have lost heart. Then an attack is put in by a mixed infantry tank company sized grouping. Due to shortage of ammo on Bosnian side, villages fall one by one and Serbs proceed to next series of villages. It is a slow remorseless and continual advance."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that reflect your understanding or at any rate your intelligence as of the 14th of March, 1993, that those offensives, Serb offences were going on in that way?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only on the 14th of March. It was our intelligence and understanding that that was the entire way that the Serb military were operating, what I referred to as the offensive earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If just -- perhaps to summarise in a way what was going on and tell me if you agree with this description, would you say it was a relentless crushing of the pocket that was being pursued?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was terrorism by artillery. It was terrorising the population of a village so that the moment the shells started dropping the villagers knew that their turn was next. The Serb -- I mean literally it was only three shells an hour. But that was enough to terrorise the population, who would then flee. Then two days later, three days later, there would be a quick sudden little Serb attack. Nothing that a journalist could observe and watch and get excited about and say, oh, there's a big offensive there, but it was remorseless. It was like, do you know the old computer game PacMan? The way we described it was the Serb PacMan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gobbling up village by village.

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Village by village. Remorseless. The issue for the refugees in Srebrenica, the ones who surrounded us, is that they -- they believed they were going to die. It was not a question of if, it was only a question of when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that is reflected on the next page, 3456. These people believe they will be killed in the next few weeks?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One final question before we break. You described the difficult conditions under which Naser Oric was operating as a commander. These were the conditions which you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: PYERS TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They and many other aspects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think that is a convenient point to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jones, and I thank you, Colonel Tucker. We will reconvene at 9.00 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of March, 2005 at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
